original_target.title: Does a bound bipolaron ever break rotational symmetry?

full_original_statement:
For $`\psi\in H^1(\mathbb R^6)`$ with $`\|\psi\|_2=1`$, set

```math
\rho_\psi(x)=\int(|\psi(x,y)|^2+|\psi(y,x)|^2)\,dy,
```



```math
\mathcal P_U(\psi)=\iint\left(|\nabla_x\psi|^2+|\nabla_y\psi|^2+\frac{U|\psi|^2}{|x-y|}\right)dx\,dy-\iint\frac{\rho_\psi(x)\rho_\psi(y)}{|x-y|}\,dx\,dy.
```

Write $`E_2(U)=\inf\mathcal P_U`$ and

```math
E_1=\inf_{\substack{\phi\in H^1(\mathbb R^3)\\\|\phi\|_2=1}}\left\{\int|\nabla\phi|^2-\iint\frac{|\phi(x)|^2|\phi(y)|^2}{|x-y|}\,dx\,dy\right\}.
```

For every $`U\ge0`$ with $`E_2(U)<2E_1`$, must every minimizer, after a common translation of its coordinates, obey

```math
\psi(Rx,Ry)=\psi(x,y)\quad\text{for every }R\in O(3)?
```

Equivalently, determine whether rotational symmetry breaking occurs anywhere in the binding regime.

sources.scope_comparison: The target quantifies over every repulsion U in the binding regime and every minimizer, modulo a common translation. The primary actual theorem assumes U<U_s for some small positive U_s and explicitly leaves possible loss of rotation invariance near Uc open. Scaling the electron–phonon coupling does not turn the small-U regime into every binding U. Numerical bipolarons or symmetry for other functionals do not settle this continuum Pekar–Tomasevich target. No later complete matching announcement was found.
